text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: Multiple 502/504 egress failures observed from services in us-east-1a (AZ1). Error spike at 2026-03-15T02:13Z. Pager sent to #oncall.
jo: seeing it too — spike in outbound connection failures to S3 and external APIs. dashboards.redwood/internal -> 5xx egress + latency.
sam: @jo oncall here, digging in. Is it just one subnet/route table?
jo: looks concentrated on subnet subnet-0a9c* in AZ1. Instances healthy, ENIs up. NAT gw metrics show high active connections and errors.
priya: tagging network: aws says NAT gateway in AZ1 <redacted-nat-id> reports >95% connection errors, unhealthy. Could be during last infra deploy at 02:08Z. deploy-bot: Completed rolling update -> infra/routing/2026-03-15T02:07Z (ids: rtb-0b12, asg-nat-proxy).
elliot: I can tail vpc flow logs for that subnet, running query now. sharing snippet: ```Filter: dstaddr != 10.0.0.0/8 AND action=REJECT | limit 50```
elliot: flow logs show lots of "REJECT" on ephemeral ports, NACL entries updated at 02:07:10Z.
jo: that matches the deploy window. I suspect an automated NACL rule add went out with the deploy.
sam: priority: mitigate customers. Quick question — can we reroute that subnet to healthy nat in AZ2, or create temporary NAT instance?
priya: we can add a route in the subnet's route table pointing 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-healthy (in another rt) but cross-AZ egress costs may rise. If route propagation uses same RT, might be sticky.
jo: trying `aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0a9c --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --instance-id i-zzzz` to point at standby NAT instance. Hold on.
jo: ERROR: route replace failed: InvalidRoute.NotFound. Looks like route table was locked by a recent change (propagation in progress).
sam: if propagation locked, second option: create a transit ENI in AZ2 and attach a temporary NAT instance in AZ1 as quick failover. Do we have a golden AMI for NAT-instance?
priya: yes: ami-0natbase in ops account. I'll spin one up in the affected subnet with source/dest check disabled and add route to it.
elliot: starting boot now, will preseed iptables/SNAT.
priya: spun up instance i-tempnat-34, source/dest check disabled, iptables SNAT set to elastic IP x.x.x.x. Adding route...
priya: route added: rtb-0a9c -> i-tempnat-34. Testing egress from an app host...
jo: initial checks — HTTP calls passing, S3 PUTs succeed. Metrics: error rate dropping from 48% -> 6% in the last 3 minutes.
sam: good. Marking mitigation=temporary NAT instance. Notify support to update customers.
oncall-bot: paging support on #support: incident impacting customers using outbound integrations in us-east-1a, mitigation in progress (temporary NAT instance).
support (via @support): acknowledged, crafting customer msg. Estimated affected customers: ~12 tenants with high egress.
deploy-bot: I see a recent infra change that added NACL rule ID nacl-change-492 at 02:07:10Z: `deny tcp 1024-65535 0.0.0.0/0` on subnet-0a9c.
jo: that's the smoking gun — ephemeral port deny. Who pushed that change?
sam: rolling back that specific change now. `aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0b123 --rule-number 100 --egress --protocol 6 --port-range From=1024,To=65535 --rule-action allow`
sam: command returned ok. Removing deny rule.
elliot: flow logs show REJECTs stop immediately after rule removal. But NAT gw is still in degraded state — connections that hit it earlier may remain stuck.
jo: leaving temp NAT instance active for 30m until NAT gateway back to healthy.
priya: noted. Updating runbook: mark as mitigated and begin recovery steps for stable NAT: contact AWS to investigate NAT gateway internal errors, open support case ID #CASE-2026-0421.
sam: on-call escalation: @priya taking over for next 2 hours, I'm handing off. Jo, Elliot — standby for verification.
jo: handing off logs and commands to Priya. Also saving a pcap snippet and flow log query.
priya: thanks. I'll monitor for 30 minutes and then remove temp NAT if everything stable. Also will escalate for postmortem: find how NACL change got into infra deploy (policy gating failed).
sam: adding followup tasks: (1) add extra CI check to block ephemeral-port-deny NACL rules, (2) update runbook with NAT-replacement steps, (3) customer comms debrief.
priya: support lead @maria looped in on customer emails. Suggested message: "We experienced intermittent egress failures in US-EAST-1a between 02:07 and 02:40 UTC due to an incorrect NACL change during a deploy. Traffic restored via temporary NAT instance; permanent remediation underway."
jo: metrics look green: 5xx back to baseline, latency normalized. I'll keep temp NAT but mark for termination at 03:10Z if stable.
priya: case opened with AWS, link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#/case/?caseId=CASE-2026-0421 (internal).
sam: great work. Closing the pager as mitigated — will convert to major incident postmortem doc.
oncall-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> active->resolved? (updated)
priya: switching to monitoring-only. Will post a short RCA draft in #postmortems in 2 hours.
sam: handing back to triage: thank you team. :thumbsup:
